about.title: Sanger Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Sanger's economy runs on agriculture, packing houses, trucking, and light industry, and each of those settings carries its own injury risks. Workers get hurt from equipment failures, repetitive strain, falls from ladders or loading docks, and vehicle incidents on routes like Academy Avenue or Bethel Avenue while making deliveries. Most of the time, workers' compensation is the only path against an employer, no matter who was at fault. But when a negligent third party — a subcontractor, a property owner, or an equipment manufacturer — contributed to the injury, a separate claim may be possible outside the workers' comp system. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly; we simply connect injured Sanger workers with an independent attorney who can look at the details, explain the deadlines that apply, and help sort out whether more than one path forward exists. There's no cost to get that conversation started, and no obligation to move forward afterward.

whyChoose.title: Why Sanger Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Third-Party Angle
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can sometimes support a separate claim. An independent attorney can help identify whether that possibility applies to your situation.

items.title: Knowing the Reporting Window
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate a claim, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Retaliation against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. An attorney can explain what protections apply if you're concerned about your job standing.

items.question: I was hurt at a packing facility near Jensen Avenue — can I still file a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: Yes, in most cases workers' compensation applies regardless of fault, and location doesn't change that. What matters more is reporting the injury to your employer within 30 days and documenting how it happened. An independent attorney can walk through the specifics with you.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for a workplace injury in Sanger?
items.answer: Generally, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against an employer in California, which means a direct lawsuit usually isn't available. However, if a third party — like an equipment manufacturer or a subcontractor on site — contributed to the injury, a separate claim against that party may be possible. An attorney can help sort out which applies to your case.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work on Academy Avenue or Annadale Avenue?
items.answer: If you were injured in a vehicle collision while on the job, workers' comp likely covers your injury, but if another driver was at fault, a third-party claim against that driver may also be available. These claims run on a separate 2-year deadline, so timing matters. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can evaluate both angles at no cost.
